blogs.title: Why Reinforcement Learning Isn’t Needed Anymore for Aligning Language Models
blogs.description: A lay‑person’s guide to the core insight of Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), showing how a clever re‑parameterization lets us skip the reward‑model and RL steps entirely. The post walks through the intuition, the math in plain English, and why this matters for building safer AI.

blogs.title: From Preferences to Policies: How DPO Turns Human Choices Into Model Behavior
blogs.description: Explains the Bradley‑Terry preference model, the traditional RLHF pipeline, and how DPO rewrites the loss as a simple binary‑cross‑entropy on the language model itself. Includes visual analogies and code snippets that demonstrate the DPO objective in practice.

blogs.title: The Theory Behind Direct Preference Optimization: Rewards Hidden Inside the Model
blogs.description: Digs into the theoretical guarantees of DPO—equivalence classes of reward functions, the closed‑form optimal policy, and why DPO’s reparameterization preserves all expressivity. Ideal for readers who love proofs but want them broken down step‑by‑step.

blogs.title: DPO vs. PPO: A Head‑to‑Head Comparison on Real‑World Tasks
blogs.description: Summarizes the experimental results from sentiment control, summarization, and dialogue. Highlights DPO’s better reward–KL trade‑off, stability, and simplicity, with charts and everyday analogies that make the numbers easy to grasp.

blogs.title: How to Deploy Direct Preference Optimization in Your Own Project
blogs.description: A practical tutorial that walks developers through setting up a preference dataset, defining a reference model, implementing the DPO loss in PyTorch/Transformers, and fine‑tuning a 2‑B parameter model. Ends with tips for hyper‑parameter selection and troubleshooting.
